findings.type: economic-quantification (extends CODE-001; do not file separately)
findings.suggestedSeverity: Low. Refutes a Medium: zero extractable value, liveness/custody only
findings.description: The front-run of the step-5 proportional exit is a grief, not an extraction. A Balancer swap moves the per-BPT composition: one leg up, one leg down. Because step 6 seeds the simulation-baked sAmt/pAmt, the outcome is binary. Either the seed lands at EXACTLY the simulation price, or the short leg's transferFrom reverts. The core can never seed at a manipulated ratio. The 1% _checkMinAmountsOut window does not bound a loss, because there is no loss mechanism. It only bounds how far the composition may shift before the Balancer Router itself reverts. The surplus leg in the reverted case stays on the OWNER EOA.
findings.economicImpact: Exiter value is monotone non-decreasing under any pre-exit swap. Valued at the pre-swap price, the 62.9% share gains x^2/(S+x)-scale value: +0.40 sUSDS for a 100-sUSDS front-run, +1.08 for 185.7 (the 1% leg edge), +83 for 2,000. The attacker's round trip on the same curve loses about 2 x 0.3% of the swap: -0.60 sUSDS at 100, -1.11 at 185.7, -11.2 at 2,000. That holds even when the back-run is optimally split across the new V2 pair and the Balancer remnant, because the proportional split preserves the combined constant-product curve. In dollars, the 1% tolerance is ~$206.6 per leg, but none of it is capturable.
findings.attackScenario:
1. OWNER broadcasts steps 1-5 under --slow --ledger at 0.3 gwei (story-103 :broadcast). That is several mined txs, which gives a multi-block window.
2. The attacker (or any of the ~5 organic swaps/week, ~1e-4 per block) swaps on 0x642B before the step-5 exit is mined.
3. sUSDS-short direction: any phUSD->sUSDS swap of a few wei shorts the sUSDS leg. OWNER holds 0 spare sUSDS, so step 6 reverts.
4. phUSD-short direction: OWNER holds 1.4727 spare phUSD, so the swap needs to short the phUSD leg by >1.47 phUSD. That is ~2.34 phUSD pool-wide, a ~1.93 sUSDS (~$2.15) swap costing ~$0.006 in fee. Below that threshold the seed SUCCEEDS by pulling up to 1.47 of OWNER's personal phUSD (<= $1.35) into POL. That is harmless.
5. Cost to the attacker: gas (~$0.03-0.15) plus <$0.01 of fee, all lost. Gain: none.
findings.profitability: Never profitable. Pure griefing at under $0.20 per attempt. Once the seed reverts it leaves the canonical pair empty. That extends the ledgered 2-wei poisoning window (9a694ae01fe1 / ycn L-26), which is the only way a griefer converts the stall into a durable brick.
findings.affectedParties: Protocol (liveness; ~$41.3k of POL in EOA custody until a hand recovery). No user or LP value loss.
findings.severityRationale: C4 Medium needs value leak or availability impact with stated assumptions. Here the availability impact is real but self-inflicted by the non-atomic core, recoverable by the owner, and it disappears when story 103 rewires onto the escrow (atomic exitAndSeed). Low is honest.
relatedLedger: yield-claim-nft L-28 d77a482de757 (same trigger against the escrow, fix-pending)

findings.type: spec-staleness (Law 2) - third-party BPT holder misidentified in story 103
findings.description: Story 103 L213 says 'BPT held by third parties (0xE74E..1322, 0x5f97..d2, 0xde44..3D07) is out of scope'. On-chain, all three hold 0 BPT. The only non-protocol holder is 0xc65faaafbbda520791f344d33497485edf58e8db, with 12,036.97 BPT: 37.1% of supply, ~10,957 sUSDS + ~13,309 phUSD, ~$24.4k. BalancerWinddownPlan.md L62-65 and open question #1 (L531, 'Known to the owner, who will contact them directly') identify that holder, but story 103 never names them. The cutover itself is FAIR to this LP. The protocol's proportional exit leaves the per-BPT claim unchanged: Balancer rounds in the pool's favour, so remaining LPs gain dust. It leaves the spot price unchanged (both balances x0.371). Recovery-mode exit after the 30 Oct pause is also proportional. After the cutover, 0xc65f is the SOLE LP of a 0.3%-fee pool at the old price, and Stage-4 pool() lifts on the V2 pair will be arbitraged into it until it pauses (ledgered as ycn Q-25 b4c10f0f8938: $8-$11).
findings.economicImpact: None from the cutover's mechanics. The risk is procedural. The story's out-of-scope bullet points the verify/report step at the wrong addresses, so the plan's 'warn the 37% LP' obligation has no story checkpoint.
findings.fix: Amend story 103's third-party bullet to name 0xc65f (12,036.97 BPT at block 26181448). Have verify print the post-cutover holder set of the Balancer pool.

findings.type: venue-depth quantification + spec gap (extends CODE-006; do not file separately)
findings.suggestedSeverity: QA/Low (unchanged). No loss when minOut is quote-derived. The trap is UI/UX
findings.description: The DOLA-3CRV metapool caps the DOLA route at about $1.5k total USDC out. DOLA->USDC: 1,000 -> 984.95 (-1.5%), 2,000 -> 1,519 (-24%), 5,000 -> 1,543 (-69%). USDC->DOLA: 2,000 -> 1,818 (-9%). The quote path calls the same pool's get_dy_underlying, so a UI minOut of quote x (1 - tol) is internally consistent and the user receives what was quoted. The route is a value trap only if the UI shows the phUSD/DOLA output without a price-impact comparison to the ~$0.916 phUSD reference. In that case the 'leak' goes to Curve LPs and rebalancing arbitrageurs, not to the protocol. Story 109 L168 explicitly asks the executor to confirm on-fork depth for USDe (it is deep: 50k -> 49,954) but asks nothing for DOLA. That gap let a near-empty venue ship. Story 109 L241 also records that USDC->DOLA get_dy_underlying over-estimates execution by ~0.002%. A zero-tolerance minOut on that direction reverts, which is fail-closed.
findings.economicImpact: A user selling 5,000 DOLA for phUSD at the quoted output gets ~$1,543 of value, a ~$3.4k haircut, with explicit quote consent. Sandwich exposure is the caller's tolerance on the final minOut. Intermediate legs carry 0 mins inside one atomic tx, which is fine.
findings.attackScenario:
1. UI quotes DOLA->phUSD through quoteToPhUSD and shows only the output amount.
2. User accepts and executes with minOut = quote x 0.99.
3. User receives ~31% of value at 5k DOLA. Arbitrageurs later rebalance the Curve pool and capture it.
findings.profitability: Third-party arbitrageurs profit from rebalancing. Nothing is extracted from protocol funds.
findings.affectedParties: Helper users on the DOLA route above ~$1k.
findings.fix: Before the story-111 broadcast, pick a deep DOLA venue (plan L186: DOLA/sUSDS on Curve is the deepest active sUSDS pool), or have the UI compute and block on price impact versus the pair spot for every route.

findings.type: plan-number drift (extends cross-project informational; not a new root cause)
findings.suggestedSeverity: Informational (update existing entries' numbers; do not file new)
findings.description: The seed price carried over by the proportional exit is 0.8233 sUSDS = $0.9160 per phUSD. For a 50/50 weighted pool, the token-unit balance ratio equals the spot price, so the V2 seed reproduces the Balancer spot exactly, as plan decision 3 intends. The seed is 8.4% below the $1 mint price. Minting is mint-only (no redemption floor), so a below-peg seed opens NO mint/sell arbitrage. Back-running the seed has no edge either: the V2 pair and the Balancer remnant start at the identical price. Since the plan's block 26,093,540, the price has fallen from 0.971 to 0.916 (the holding pattern stopped pool() on 2026-10-01). The live crossing Delta* on the seeded pair is 1,895 USDS, against the plan's ~$640 and F-03-052's $1,712. Using the stale figure for the 'first call about Delta*' errs SAFE (undershoot, no arb skim). Pooling the whole post-cutover sUSDS balance at once (1,957.66 sUSDS = 2,178 USDS) overshoots by ~$283, lifts phUSD to ~$1.0125, and costs about $0.2 of arb skim (~141 phUSD minted, which is collateral the no-ceiling design wants). Negligible.
findings.economicImpact: None material. The stale numbers err in the safe direction.
findings.fix: Refresh plan section 5 / Stage 4 step 6 figures from a live read at broadcast time. That is the existing F-03-052 recommendation.

clearedChecks.item: Q2 sandwich around step 6 / back-run after seeding (core)
clearedChecks.verdict: Cleared. Step 6 seeds an EMPTY pair at baked amounts, so there is no price to sandwich. The only pre-seed interaction with the pair is first-LP poisoning (ledgered 9a694ae01fe1). The seed equals the Balancer spot at simulation. Any Balancer drift before the exit reverts step 6 (ECON-001) rather than mispricing it. A Balancer remnant swap between step 5 and step 6 opens a cross-venue gap paid for by the swapper. That is ordinary LVR on $41k of POL, cents-scale.

clearedChecks.item: Q2/Q6 escrow whole-balance seed + 1-wei exit floor (yield-claim-nft Q-24 / L-28)
clearedChecks.verdict: No economic escalation. With the escrow, the seed ratio FOLLOWS the exit composition. A front-run therefore shifts the V2 seed price: ~+-2% at the 1% floor, unbounded with 1-wei floors. Even so, the proportional exit plus whole-balance seed keeps the combined (V2 + remnant) constant-product curve intact. The attacker's sandwich is a round trip on that curve and loses about 0.6% of notional (simulated -0.06 to -11.2 sUSDS for 10 to 2,000 sUSDS front-runs, optimal split back-run). The protocol's value at the pre-attack price strictly rises, because the invariant only grows. The 1-wei floor matters for liveness and hygiene only (ycn L-28 / Q-24, already ledgered). Holds because the pool is 50/50 weighted and both exit modes are proportional.

clearedChecks.item: Q4 index-4 mints during the windows
clearedChecks.verdict: Availability only, no user value lost. ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch is onlyMinter, called inside the NFTMinterV2 mint tx, so a hook OnlyDispatcher revert (CODE-003) unwinds the whole mint: the user keeps their USDS, loses gas, and the price curve does not advance. Debt accrued between step 7 and step 8 stays on the hook (mintDebt), owed to NFTStaker, not lost. Interim mints that wrap onto the old pooler after the baked step-11 rescue (CODE-002) leave PROTOCOL sUSDS idle on the paused old pooler. That is recoverable via the not-pause-gated rescueERC20, so it is opportunity cost, not loss.

Correct. _quoteToSusds mirrors DssLitePsm sellGem (usds = gem x conv - usds x tin / WAD). psmGemForUsds inverts buyGem cost with a floor, and the remainder is refunded to the recipient. Live tin = tout = 0. If Sky sets tin to the HALTED sentinel (uint max), the quote overflows and reverts, and so does sellGem. Fail-closed, consistent.

clearedChecks.item: Q5 quote path soundness for the UI
clearedChecks.verdict: Sound as a spot quote. Every leg quotes the exact venue it executes on (V2 getAmountsOut, Curve get_dy(_underlying), QuoterV2, previewDeposit/Redeem). It is intra-block manipulable like any spot quote, but the executed minOut is the guard. Note the documented ~0.002% optimistic bias on USDC->DOLA (story 109 L241): the UI tolerance must be > 0. The ETH quotes are non-view (eth_call only).

clearedChecks.item: Q5 route mispriced by design / helper vs minter
clearedChecks.verdict: No. The helper buys phUSD only from the V2 pair, never via PhusdStableMinter (1:1, no fee). Today the pair (0.916) is cheaper than minting, which favours the user. Above peg (intended, no ceiling), a helper buyer can pay up to the arb band (~0.3% fee + gas) over the $1 mint. That is bounded and quote-consented. Not reported.
Not applicable. No recommendation touches the commingled cap.

notes: No new High/Medium. Every cutover economic vector reduces to liveness/custody (CODE-001/003, ycn L-28) or to ledgered hygiene.

Key structural reason: the Balancer pool is 50/50 weighted, so a proportional exit plus a ratio-preserving seed is value-neutral to the combined curve. Every sandwich is a fee-paying round trip. If the pool were a stable/ECLP pool, this conclusion would NOT hold, so re-check it if a non-weighted pool is ever cut over the same way.
ECON-001, ECON-003 and ECON-004 extend existing items and should be merged by the deduplicator, not filed. ECON-002 is the only new entry (QA, spec-conformance).
